subject: AWS Marketplace metering & fulfillment: entitlement points and procurement checklist
messages:
From: Terri Lowe <terri@orpheus.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orpheus.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on AWS Marketplace metering & procurement timeline

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're finalizing our procurement plan and need to confirm a couple of technical and commercial items before we can issue a PO and move forward with listing on AWS Marketplace (co-sell). High level items below — can you confirm by EOD Monday?

1) Metering metric + entitlement mapping: we bill our customers by monthly active seats and want to understand the best way to map our seat licensing to AWS Marketplace entitlements (metering dimensions, granularity, and whether Redwood supports per-tenant SKU mapping).
2) Fulfillment payload: sample JSON we should expect from Redwood fulfillment for usage events (we'll hand to our billing ops).
3) SLA and fallback behavior: what happens if Redwood is unable to reach Seller Central for metering? Any buffering / retry behavior?
4) Procurement docs: we'll need a redlineable Annex A with SOC/PII language and an initial DocuSign for the SaaS addendum + PO routing instructions (procurement@orpheus.ai).

Attaching our procurement checklist (stub) so you can see the timeline constraints — we need a signed route by 12/22 to make Q1 credits. Also please loop in your AWS marketplace enablement contact if there are any seller-central prerequisites.

Appreciate it — Terri

--
Terri Lowe
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Orpheus Analytics
terri@orpheus.ai

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Terri Lowe <terri@orpheus.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, aws-seller-central@amazon.com
Date: 2026-12-10T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on AWS Marketplace metering & procurement timeline

Terri — thanks, and great to see the checklist. Short answers up front, details below and next steps at the bottom.

Quick summary:
- Entitlements: we support per-tenant SKU mapping and recommend a single boolean "active_seat" dimension per customer plus an optional integer "seat_count" if you need usage-based aggregation.
- Fulfillment payload: attaching a sample payload and an XLS with field mappings (Redwood_AWS_Fulfillment_Specs.xlsx).
- Retries/buffering: Redwood buffers usage events locally and will retry up to 72 hours; after that we fall back to a reconciliation job and create an invoice-facing delta if Seller Central rejects events.
- Docs: attaching a draft Annex A and a DocuSign route will be created once procurement confirms primary signer (we can prefill).

Details:
1) Metering & entitlements: For co-sell we recommend using an entitlement per AWS account (AWS account ID -> Redwood tenant ID) and minting a corresponding Marketplace SKU. If you prefer monthly seat aggregates, include the "seat_count" integer in each metering event; Redwood will roll up at the interval defined in your Seller Central settings.

2) Example fulfillment event (JSON snippet) is in the XLS; main fields: timestamp, tenant_id, aws_account_id, sku_id, metric_name, quantity, metadata (freeform). We also include an "event_source" field so your billing ops can trace if it came from streaming vs. reconciliation.

3) Failure modes: primary path is synchronous push to AWS Marketplace. If push fails we buffer locally and attempt exponential backoff for 72 hours. If the event still cannot be delivered we surface a reconciliation report and will create compensating usage records on the next monthly sweep. We'll surface all failures in the Redwood Console with per-tenant audit logs.

4) Procurement & legal: We'll attach Annex A (draft) and can accept your redlines. For SOC2 evidence we can provide our summary report and add an exhibit referencing our SOC2 assessor — Soojin, can you attach the latest SOC2 snapshot?

Next steps (proposed):
A) You confirm primary signer for DocuSign (procurement@orpheus.ai) by 12/13.
B) We send Annex A + DocuSign link and your team returns redlines.
C) Integration kickoff week of 12/20 (30-60m tech call with your billing ops and our integrations engineer).

Attachments: Redwood_AWS_Fulfillment_Specs.xlsx (field mappings + sample payload), Annex_A_SaaS_Terms_Draft.pdf (stub)

Happy to jump on a 30m call if you'd prefer to walk through the payload.

Thanks — Diego

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Partner Engineer, Marketplace
Redwood Inference
